explanation: A dense English 'explain-it-to-the-reader' detector: it runs high across nearly every token of prose that characterises, qualifies or advises about a general subject (lesson/explainer material, how-to guides, product descriptions, assistant answers, research abstracts) and sits at zero through narrative fiction, news reports, encyclopedic entries about a particular entity, impersonal lab-method descriptions, recipes, maths and code. Wherever it fires, its peaks are on the words doing the characterising or qualifying: abstract assessment nouns (advantages, characteristics, examples, description, methods, topics, objectives, steps, listed, required), the copula and participle of a descriptive predicate (are, given), the prepositions that attach a description to its subject (of, by, into, through) and negations/quantifiers (not, n't, without, all, more, any) - so a qualifying clause fires even inside a narrative, but only the descriptive register keeps the surrounding tokens above zero.
